Yemen’s Houthis say they attacked Saudi Rabigh oil refinery

Reuters

22 November, 2026 11:30 pm IST

Nov 22 (Reuters) – Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Sunday they had carried out an operation targeting Saudi Arabia’s Rabigh oil refinery on the kingdom’s western Red Sea coast, as they continued to claim attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

The Houthis said they had achieved a direct hit but there was no indication of what damage had been inflicted and the Saudi authorities did not immediately comment.

Rabigh is home to Petro Rabigh, a major integrated oil refining and petrochemical complex developed by Saudi Aramco and Japan’s Sumitomo Chemical. It is located about 165 km north of Jeddah on the Red Sea coast and has access to deep-water export facilities.

Show Full Article

The Houthis have repeatedly claimed attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure in recent months, including the East-West oil pipeline and refineries in Jazan in the south and Ras Tanura in Eastern Province. Saudi authorities have not confirmed any attacks on refineries.

The renewed fighting, which began in July amid the wider US-Israeli war with Iran, has seen the Houthis seize territory from Yemen’s internationally recognised government and step up missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and energy infrastructure.

Saudi Arabia has also intensified airstrikes against Houthi positions in support of its Yemeni allies.

(Reporting by Hatem Maher and Ahmed Tolba; Editing by Susan Fenton and David Holmes)

US seeks answers on Nvidia’s sale of chips to China, Bessent says

Reuters

By Katharine Jackson WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) – The US is seeking answers from Nvidia on its chip sales to China and will find out who was in charge of compliance at the company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday.

“We’ve been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers. … It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Bessent told the CBS program “Face the Nation.”

Reports about Huang’s relationship with a woman whom US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy and his extramarital affair with a company executive led to his resignation and investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.

Show Full Article

Days after Huang’s resignation, President Donald Trump’s administration issued a rule to further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening controls ahead of Trump’s trip to China last week for talks with President Xi Jinping.

Bessent said the chipmaker’s board of directors is working to determine what had happened, and he expressed confidence that it would “come up with some very fulsome and robust answers.”

“We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there,” Bessent said. “We will see which level of the business knew about this. Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle level? Did it go all the way to the top?”

Trump said on Friday that he would like to see Huang apologize and return to Nvidia. Asked whether he agreed with Trump, Bessent said more information is needed.

“I think we have to see where the buck stops,” Bessent said.

Nvidia board Chairman Harvey Jones has said the board will not rehire Huang.

(Reporting by Katharine Jackson; Editing by Sergio Non, Will Dunham and Bill Berkrot)

Reuters

By John Kruzel WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) – Russian President Vladimir Putin is not a friend when it comes to Ukraine, US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Sunday, days after President Donald Trump spoke warmly of Russia’s leader.

“He is not America’s friend in Ukraine,” Clayton told ABC News’ “This Week” program. “Not at all.”

Asked about Trump’s recent description of Putin as a friend, Clayton also said the term was “entirely appropriate” in the context of discussions among leaders of the world’s three leading nuclear powers — the United States, Russia and China — during last week’s high-profile summit in China.

Show Full Article

Trump defended calling Putin a friend on Thursday, saying that “it’s nice to have people that have 4,000 nuclear weapons as a friend as opposed to an enemy.” But when asked about the subject again on Friday, Trump declined to say whether Putin is a friend to the United States as a whole: “I can’t speak to America.”

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and controls about a fifth of the country’s territory. Putin has shown no sign of dropping his demand that Ukraine surrender all of its eastern Donbas region in exchange for peace.

Trump’s description of Putin as a friend drew criticism from European allies of Ukraine. “Mr Putin is not our friend and will never be,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.

Asked on Thursday about Trump’s remarks, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy shrugged and walked away.

(Reporting by John Kruzel; Editing by Sergio Non and Bill Berkrot)
